t: Field-Level Equivalence Detector: a plain-language overview
title: Field-Level Equivalence Detector: a plain-language overview
description: Overview: what the Field-Level Equivalence Detector does and why archives need it. A field-level equivalence detector finds columns that secretly mean the same thing: 'zip', 'postal_code', and 'zipcode' are one field wearing three disguises. It compares the actual values inside the columns — if two columns hold the same kind of data, they are probably the same field. Different names, same meaning, one truth.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Field-Level Equivalence Detector works
title: How the Field-Level Equivalence Detector works
description: Overview: what the Field-Level Equivalence Detector does and why archives need it. Real detectors compare fields by value overlap (Jaccard on sampled values), value-pattern similarity (both match the ZIP regex), name similarity, and co-occurrence (fields that appear together in the same tables). Evidence fuses into an equivalence score; pairs above threshold become equivalence groups, and groups merge transitively with a consistency check. Each group lists its member fields, the evidence per pair, and a canonical name proposal.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.

t: How the Field-Level Equivalence Detector works: the deep tour
title: How the Field-Level Equivalence Detector works: the deep tour
description: Overview: what the Field-Level Equivalence Detector does and why archives need it. Real detectors compare fields by value overlap (Jaccard on sampled values), value-pattern similarity (both match the ZIP regex), name similarity, and co-occurrence (fields that appear together in the same tables). Evidence fuses into an equivalence score; pairs above threshold become equivalence groups, and groups merge transitively with a consistency check. Each group lists its member fields, the evidence per pair, and a canonical name proposal. Advanced detectors use distributional embeddings of column values, handle unit differences (one column in miles, another in kilometers) by detecting convertible distributions, and validate groups against known business rules. Quality is measured by group precision/recall on labeled multi-source warehouses. The limits are coincidentally similar columns (two unrelated ID columns with overlapping ranges) — the detector requires multi-signal agreement and reports borderline groups for review rather than merging on one signal.
provenance: Public methods compiled from standard information-extraction and knowledge-organization practice. Assembled for the JAH Databases archive.
